what_its_for: Suvorexant is a sleep medicine used to help adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep (insomnia). It works by blocking signals in the brain that keep you awake, helping your body transition into sleep naturally.
how_to_take: Take suvorexant by mouth as a tablet. Swallow it whole with or without food. Take it only when you are ready to go to bed and you have at least 7 hours before you need to wake up. Do not take it unless you can get a full night of sleep. Never take more than one dose in a single night.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken once per night, no more than 30 minutes before bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to a maximum of 20 mg per night if needed. Always take the lowest dose that works for you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: Suvorexant is taken only when needed at bedtime, so there is no regular schedule to follow. If you forget to take it before bed but you still have at least 7 hours before you need to wake up, you may take it then. If it is almost time to wake up, skip the dose completely. Never take two doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store suvorexant at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely, preferably through a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking suvorexant — it can dangerously increase drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires full alertness the morning after taking this medicine, as you may still feel drowsy. Do not take other sleep medicines, sedatives, or anti-anxiety medications without your doctor's approval. Avoid taking it with a heavy meal, as this may delay how quickly it works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: sleepwalking or doing other activities while asleep (such as eating, driving, or making phone calls) without remembering it; worsening depression or thoughts of suicide or self-harm; hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); sleep paralysis (unable to move when waking up); unusual or vivid dreams; severe allergic reactions such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if your sleep problems do not improve or get worse after 7 to 10 days.
when_it_works: Suvorexant usually starts working within 30 minutes of taking it. Most people notice improvement in their sleep within the first few nights, but it may take up to a few weeks to feel the full benefit. If your sleep does not improve after 7 to 10 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, including drowsiness and dizziness, which can increase the risk of falls. Use extra caution. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Breastfeeding: It is not known if suvorexant passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, this medicine may not be safe for you. Tell your doctor about any liver conditions. Children: Suvorexant is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 18 years of age.
